items.title: Interview with a Classmate: Danya Mubarak
items.label: Featured Interview
items.excerpt: An 11-year-old horse-riding enthusiast shares her dreams of becoming a coach and her love for swimming.
items.body:
This week, our reporter Fatima Almusaifri sat down with Danya Mubarak from Grade 5C to learn more about her hobbies, dreams, and daily life.

Danya is 11 years old and lives in Duhail with her parents and two younger sisters. As the oldest of three, she says she loves being a big sister — though she admits she'd like another little sister too.

Her biggest passion is horse-riding. She started riding in January 2024, and she now goes to practice every week. "Horse-riding makes me feel strong and free," she says. "When I'm on a horse, I forget about everything else."

Danya also loves swimming. She's good at both sports, but horse-riding is her true love. When she grows up, she wants to become a horse-riding coach — to teach other kids the sport she loves.

Her favorite colors are purple and pink. Her favorite subjects are PE and history. And her best friends at Albayan are Fatima, Reem, and Joud.

When asked to describe herself in three words, Danya didn't hesitate: "Confident. Strong. Smart."

We couldn't agree more.
items.author: Fatima Almusaifri

items.title: A Day in the Life of a Grade 6 Student
items.label: Student Voice
items.excerpt: What does it take to balance studies, hobbies, and friendships in your final year at Albayan?
items.body:
We spoke with a Grade 6 student about what life looks like in the final year at Albayan.

"Grade 6 is busy — but it's also the best year," she told us. "You know everyone, you know the teachers, and you feel ready for what's next."

A typical day starts with waking up at 6 AM, breakfast, and arriving at school by 7. Mornings are for math and English. After lunch, there are science and Arabic classes. After school, there's homework, then a break, then more homework.

"I try to keep my weekends free for friends and family," she says. "Balance is important."

When we asked what she'd tell younger students, she said: "Enjoy every year. It goes faster than you think. And be kind to your teachers — they work so hard for us."

Her advice is simple and true.
items.author: Albayan Reporters

items.title: Behind the Scenes with Our Teachers
items.label: Teacher Spotlight
items.excerpt: An inside look at what inspires our teachers to shape the next generation every single day.
items.body:
We sat down with several of our teachers to ask them a simple question: why do you teach?

"Because of the students," one teacher said immediately. "Every day is different. Every student has something new to teach me."

Another teacher told us about a student who struggled with reading in Grade 3 and now, in Grade 6, writes her own stories. "That's why I teach," she said. "To see that growth."

We asked what advice they'd give students. The answers were consistent:

"Read. Read everything. Books open worlds."

"Ask questions. Curiosity is the best skill you can have."

"Be kind. To your classmates, to your teachers, to yourself."

We're grateful for the teachers who make Albayan such a special place.
items.author: Albayan Reporters
